obligation: GLBA Safeguards Rule (Title IV institutions): Higher Education
basis: The college agreed in its Program Participation Agreement to comply with 16 CFR Part 314, which FSA enforces (Electronic Announcement GENERAL-23-09). It holds customer information on about 1.4 million consumers, so the 314.6 exception for fewer than 5,000 consumers is not available. 314.4(a)(1)-(3) do not apply because the Qualified Individual is a college employee

obligation: GLBA Safeguards Rule: Education Software
applies: Yes (by contract, as a service provider)
basis: Education Software is a service provider to about 900 colleges, including Title IV institutions, which must require safeguards by contract; the standard college contract carries a safeguards schedule

obligation: GLBA Safeguards Rule: Student Health
basis: Student Health is not a financial institution and does not administer student aid

obligation: GLBA Safeguards Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Corporate provides the common controls the college inherits for its customer information

obligation: FERPA: Higher Education
basis: The college receives funds under Department of Education programs (34 CFR 99.1); its SIS, LMS, warehouse and campus clinic records are education records

obligation: FERPA: Education Software
applies: Yes (by contract, as a school official)
basis: Education Software keeps education records for about 6,300 customer institutions, including the college, as a contractor under their direct control

obligation: FERPA: Student Health
basis: Student Health runs the 22 campus clinics for the college and 58 clinics for 37 contracting institutions; records of their students are those institutions' education or treatment records. Group legal confirmed the record status on 2026-08-14

obligation: FERPA: corporate shared services
applies: Yes (as operator of the warehouse for the college)
basis: Corporate operates the student data warehouse and integration hub that hold the college's education records

obligation: Title IV program requirements: Higher Education
citation: Program Participation Agreement; SAIG Enrollment Agreement; 34 CFR 668.16(c); HEA sec. 483
basis: The college participates in Title IV under one PPA and holds a SAIG Enrollment Agreement. Not applicable to Education Software, Student Health or the group

obligation: Campus emergency notification: Higher Education
basis: A Title IV institution with 22 campuses must immediately notify the campus community on confirmation of a significant emergency

obligation: COPPA Rule (also N51-R02): Education Software
basis: The District Platform is used by children under 13 in about 4,100 districts, so Education Software is an operator under 16 CFR 312.2

obligation: COPPA Rule: Higher Education, Student Health and the group
basis: The college enrolls no children under 13; Student Health and corporate offer no online service directed to children

obligation: CIPA (E-Rate): all divisions
basis: No division receives E-Rate funds. The District Platform supports customers' filtering, which is the customers' duty

obligation: HIPAA hybrid entity designation: Higher Education and Student Health
basis: The college performs no covered functions; Student Health is a separate legal entity whose components all perform covered functions

obligation: CIRCIA (proposed): all divisions
basis: Not a final rule. The proposed rule would cover every Title IV institution; tracked for planning

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Student Health
basis: Student Health bills health plans electronically, so it is a health care provider that is a covered entity (45 CFR 160.103). No size exemption; 164.306(b) affects how, not whether

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Corporate creates, receives, maintains or transmits Student Health ePHI on shared services under the 2024 intercompany BAA

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Higher Education and Education Software
basis: Neither performs covered functions or acts as Student Health's business associate. Student records kept for the college are FERPA records and are excluded from PHI

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Student Health
basis: Covered entity. Applies to PHI of nonstudent patients and of all patients at the 16 community urgent care sites

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Uses and disclosures limited to the intercompany BAA

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: Student Health
basis: Own notices to nonstudent patients, HHS and media as a covered entity

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Notice to Student Health as its business associate

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM (2025): Student Health and the group
basis: Not a final rule; tracked for planning

obligation: 42 CFR Part 2 (SUD records): all divisions
basis: No division operates a federally assisted substance use disorder program

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule: all divisions
basis: Student Health is a HIPAA covered entity, which 16 CFR 318.1 excludes; no division offers a personal health record

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools: Student Health
basis: The urgent care sites accept Medicaid, which is federal financial assistance; EHR decision support tools and the AI scribe are in use

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools: Higher Education and Education Software
basis: Neither operates a health program that uses patient care decision support tools

obligation: CMS emergency preparedness conditions: Student Health
basis: Student Health's clinics are student health, counseling and urgent care clinics, not hospitals or another certified provider type that the conditions cover

obligation: HIPAA applicability to social assistance: all divisions
basis: No division is a social assistance organization

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: all divisions and the group
applies: Yes (Education Software directly; general for the others; limited for Student Health)
basis: Security, privacy, access and AI claims on the Education Software trust page and in marketing; vendor claims the college relies on

obligation: California CCPA/CPRA and CPPA regulations (including ADMT): all divisions
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq.; 11 CCR 7000 et seq. (ADMT 11 CCR 7200 et seq.)
applies: Not assessed in this sample (counsel review)
basis: Comprehensive state consumer privacy laws for Education Software are tracked by privacy counsel. The college is a for-profit business with California online students; counsel is reviewing whether the ADMT rules reach admissions scoring (raised in P10)

obligation: DOJ Data Security Program: all divisions and the group
basis: The group holds bulk sensitive personal data of students, children and patients; vendors and offshore contractors must be screened. Education Software applies it directly; the college, Student Health and corporate through vendor screening

obligation: FedRAMP: Education Software
basis: No federal agency customers

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure: group
basis: The holding company is an SEC registrant; divisions contribute incident facts through the disclosure committee

obligation: Colorado SB26-189 (automated decision-making technology): Higher Education and Education Software
basis: Deployer duties for the college's admissions scoring of Colorado online applicants; developer duties for analytics features sold to Colorado customers. Student Health falls in the carve-out for HIPAA covered entities, except employment decisions

obligation: Civil rights laws for AI in admissions and student services: Higher Education
citation: Title VI; Title IX; Section 504; Age Discrimination Act
basis: The college receives federal financial assistance and uses scoring models that affect applicants and students

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification): all divisions
basis: The group holds personal information of Florida residents; other states' breach laws apply where affected individuals reside, with Florida as the worked example. Florida personal information includes medical information

obligation: State recording consent laws (Florida worked example): Student Health
basis: The AI scribe records clinic visits; state recording laws such as Florida's (the worked example) need the consent of all parties

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 (CUI): all divisions
basis: No federal research contracts and no CUI

obligation: PCI DSS: Higher Education and Student Health
basis: Tuition card payments use a hosted payment page and clinic copays use point-to-point encrypted terminals, so card data does not enter group systems

obligation: Intercompany service agreement: the college and Education Software
basis: Sets hosting and service levels for the college tenant; contains no safeguards, notice or right-to-assess terms

obligation: Intercompany BAA: corporate shared services and Student Health
basis: Signed 2024; sets corporate's permitted uses and notice duties

obligation: Clinic services agreement and contract clinic management agreements: Student Health
basis: School-official and redisclosure terms with the college (2024) and 37 contracting institutions; incident notice terms vary by contract

obligation: Customer contracts and state student data terms: Education Software
basis: 72-hour incident notice in standard contracts; about 1,300 district contracts with state-specific terms; subprocessor and school authorization terms

obligation: SOC 2 Type 2 commitments: Education Software
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; customer contracts
applies: Yes (Education Software annually); Higher Education and Student Health out of scope
basis: Customers rely on the annual report for Security, Availability and Confidentiality
